decision: Current source implements live intermission with frozen team scoring, not a frozen simulation. Post-score AI/movement/combat outputs remain observable by the unchanged client. Removing them is a gameplay/protocol/presentation behavior change, not established dead work. No sound minimal gameplay-preserving skip was identified under this order; do not implement a speculative server-only freeze to improve fixture timing.
designIntentLimit: Encoded behavior is source-grounded below. This does not claim an external author statement, product approval for a new freeze policy, or a newly reproduced native failure.

callerTrace.runtimeConstruction: sim/loopback.ts:57 constructs the ordinary RoomEngine. Its automatic timer calls advance at70; its manual test driver calls advance at92. No alternate authored runtime constructor was found by git grep.
callerTrace.advance: sim/room-engine.ts:910-920 advances fixed ticks, flushes events, and broadcasts snapshots; input/clock/reset and network publication share this boundary.
callerTrace.step: sim/room-engine.ts:925-1031 consumes human queues, runs existing boat brains, movement and combat, performs vehicle bookkeeping, then updateMatch. The ordinary branch gates updateScores on matchEndedAt===null, not the earlier live-boat loops; the hostBridge branch is separate and boat mode rejects that bridge.
callerTrace.births: sim/room-engine.ts:updateBots returns during intermission at472, suppressing new bot births; this is distinct from existing live-brain processing earlier in step.
callerTrace.reset: sim/room-engine.ts:1128-1133 checks the existing15s room-time delay; resetMatch1169-1192 clears player ownership/stats/controls, vehicles/combat/scores, and starts the next round. It does not clear the input queues/jitter protocol state.

sourceEvidence.fact: Human input remains accepted after score end. onVehicleDestroyed still updates deaths and personal kills, but returns before teamKills increments once matchEndedAt is non-null.
sourceEvidence.quote: if (kp) kp.info.kills++; if (this.matchEndedAt !== null) return; this.teamKills[killerTeam]++
sourceEvidence.qualification: Quote condenses adjacent source lines; not a new implementation. The existing objective result is protected independently of ongoing combat.

sourceEvidence.fact: Alive local vehicles stay in flying state; flying checks paused/alive, not intermission. Frame input and local/replay stepFlight prediction continue, including the boat collision adapter.
The match-end handler calls hud.endScreen only. It does not pause, clear input, release pointer lock, remove prediction or enter a frozen state.
endScreen displays result text and schedules hide after9000 wall milliseconds. It is HUD presentation, not simulation ownership.
HUD has pointer-events:none; result styles change display/background but do not disable the Input object or change the controller state. Source styles alone are not native interaction proof.
Projectile rendering continues and extrapolates actual projectile positions/age and emits disappearance feedback; there is no intermission guard for this consumer.
The intermission flag explicitly blocks spawning and labels the next-round countdown. That flag is not an existing movement/prediction freeze contract.

rejectedMinimalSkips.candidate: Whole boat-step early return while still incrementing room time and checking reset
rejectedMinimalSkips.reason: Would also bypass consumeTick/acks, cleanup and other ongoing state consumers unless those are split out. The still-active client would continue sending inputs; the existing reset does not clear queue/jitter state. Backlog behavior would differ.
rejectedMinimalSkips.qualification: Source-derived risk, not a runtime defect reproduced by applying this rejected patch.

rejectedMinimalSkips.candidate: Skip only existing boat AI requests
rejectedMinimalSkips.reason: The last flight request remains stored; seat triggers eventually use STALE_INPUT handling, while movement still consumes stored pilot.flight. Without an explicit neutral/freeze policy, AI path avoidance, motion and fire differ. Choosing neutral requests would itself change observable post-score behavior.

rejectedMinimalSkips.candidate: Skip boat motion/combat after consuming input queues
rejectedMinimalSkips.reason: The current client still predicts local movement, exposes live input/weapon hints, and extrapolates projectiles. Server-only frozen authoritative state would change that agreement and stop observable post-score events/stats. Preserving a future freeze requires an explicit shared client/server policy, not this minimal optimization.
